edits.find: An elderly man with dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, and a gurgling sound in the neck has a Zenker diverticulum: a pulsion pouch through the weak posterior hypopharyngeal wall because the cricopharyngeus fails to relax. Order a barium esophagram first; a blind endoscope or nasogastric tube can enter the pouch and perforate it.

edits.find: Age at presentation narrows the differential. Minutes to hours: TEF/EA, choanal atresia, diaphragmatic hernia, respiratory distress syndrome, Potter sequence. Beyond 24 hours: neonatal abstinence, sepsis, ductal-dependent lesions as the PDA closes, bilious vomiting and malrotation. 3 to 6 weeks: hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Months: H-type fistula, laryngomalacia. Each wrong option here is a real disease that presents at a different age.
edits.with: Age at presentation narrows the differential. Minutes to hours: TEF (tracheoesophageal fistula) with EA (esophageal atresia), choanal atresia, diaphragmatic hernia, respiratory distress syndrome, Potter sequence. Beyond 24 hours: neonatal abstinence, sepsis, ductal-dependent lesions as the PDA (patent ductus arteriosus) closes, bilious vomiting and malrotation. 3 to 6 weeks: hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Months: H-type fistula, laryngomalacia.
